This introduction tells us that everything in this universe glorifies Allah. However, from among the things that glorify Him in this universe, those that have been selected are in harmony with the theme and central focus of this surah, and are closely connected with it. The name of the surah is Al-Jumu'ah (The Congregation). It teaches the importance of Friday: on that day, one should be free from all affairs and turn toward Allah, and at the time of the Friday prayer, one should leave off play, amusement, labour and trade and come to the remembrance of Allah. The owner of the merchandise that people have abandoned the Friday and the Friday sermon to chase after is Allah, who is the absolute King. The wealth of this world is in His control, and He is "Al-Quddus" (The Most Holy). He is sacred and pure, and the entire universe proclaims His purity and sanctity, while these people abandon His sanctification and rush toward play, amusement and trade. He is "Al-'Aziz" (The Mighty): the One who is issuing the challenge of mubahalah (mutual imprecation) to the Jews is the one who prevails. He gathers all people and arranges their reckoning and accountability. And He is "Al-Hakim" (The All-Wise): the One who raised up a Messenger from an unlettered people such as the Arabs, who recites the verses to them, teaches them wisdom and knowledge, and teaches them the Book and wisdom. The purpose of the Friday sermon is also this. In short, the attributes mentioned at the beginning are the direction in which the theme of the surah also runs.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 62, verse 2:

It has been said that the Arabs were called ummi (unlettered) because they generally did not know how to read or write. It is narrated from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "The month is like this, like this, and like this," and he gestured three times with his ten fingers, and then said: "We are an ummi nation; we do not calculate and we do not write accounts." (Al-Jassas)

It has also been said that one who does not read or write is called ummi because he is in the state in which his mother bore him, since reading and writing are acquired only by learning afterwards.

It is also possible that the Arabs were called ummi because the Jews called other nations "Goyim." In Hebrew, goyim refers to nations. They believed that they alone were the people pleasing to God, while other peoples were the common nations, that is, the ummam. Thus they called the Arabs ummi. The meaning that ummi is related to ummah (nation) appears more fitting than the meaning that it is related to umm (mother).

The Jews firmly believed that the final Prophet (ﷺ) would be raised from among them, that he would end the differences among them, that those who had been defeated by other nations in the world would be granted victory, that they would regain honour in place of humiliation, and that through the blessing of that Prophet they would win against the Arabs. Hence they used to pray for victory over the Arabs.

The wisdom of God required that the final Prophet (ﷺ) be born among the Arabs. The ummiyyin among the non-Jews were needed for the leadership of all humanity, as will be seen in the second paragraph of this surah. And just as was mentioned in Surah al-Saff, these people had gone astray, had adopted negligence and crookedness in their thinking and outlook, and in light of what they had done with God's trust throughout their long history, they were no longer fit to be entrusted with the final trust.

In this region, Prophet Ibrahim (peace be upon him) had also established a center of da'wah, and the beginning of the call was made in the shade of the House of God by Khalil Allah and his son Ismail (peace be upon him).

﴿And when Ibrahim and Ismail were raising the foundations of the House, they prayed: "Our Lord, accept this from us. Indeed You are the Hearing, the Knowing. Our Lord, make us Muslims [submitting to You], and from our descendants a nation Muslim [submitting to You]; show us our rites and forgive us. Indeed You are the Accepting of repentance, the Merciful. Our Lord, raise among them a messenger from themselves who will recite to them Your verses, teach them the Book and wisdom, and purify them. Indeed You are the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (2:127–129)

This supplication was present behind the veils of the unseen, centuries earlier, preserved with God. It was not lost. It was kept until the time that God had fixed in His wisdom had arrived. When the time fixed by His wisdom came, God accepted the prayer, the Messenger came, and the acceptance of the prayer was fulfilled, because in God's system of decree and destiny every matter occurs at its appointed time, neither before nor after.

Thus this supplication became a reality according to God's system of decree and destiny. It is here accepted in the very words in which Ibrahim had made it. The words of Ibrahim were:

﴿Our Lord, raise among them a messenger from themselves...﴾ up to ﴿...and wisdom﴾ (2:129). In praise and description of God, Ibrahim had said this.

﴿Indeed You are the...﴾ up to ﴿...the Wise.﴾ The same words are repeated here:

﴿...the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (2:129). When the Messenger of God (ﷺ) was asked about himself, he said: "I am the answer to the prayer of my father Ibrahim, the good news of Isa (peace be upon him). When my mother conceived me, she saw in a dream that a light came out from her which illuminated the palaces of Busra in the land of Sham." (Narrated by Ibn Ishaq, whose chain Ibn Kathir described as sound.)

﴿It is He who raised among the unlettered a messenger from themselves, who recites to them His verses, purifies them, and teaches them the Book and wisdom, although before that they were in clear error.﴾ (62:2)

It is a great favour of God that He raised among the unlettered a messenger from among themselves, and by giving him the Book, made them also people of the Book. From among them He made a messenger, and through him their station was elevated. He brought them out of unlettered-ness and ummiyyah: instead of being illiterate, He made them educated, and instead of being a common people (goyim), He made them an distinguished nation. He changed their circumstances, and they became distinguished people of the whole world.

﴿And purifies them﴾ (62:2). What Islam taught them was purification and cleansing: purification of conscience and awareness, purification of conduct and behaviour, purification of family life, purification of collective life, and purification of beliefs, such that all polytheistic creeds were removed and only the one creed of Tawhid was given. All false notions were eliminated and only the correct and true creed of Tawhid was bestowed. In place of fabulous ideas and beliefs, clear and certain beliefs were given. Likewise, they were delivered from moral anarchy and raised to the level of faith-based morality. In the economy, in place of the impure system of usury, they were shown the just method of lawful sustenance. In sum, a comprehensive purification was arranged, and individuals, the community, and both outward and inward life were all purified. Man was raised above this earthly life and earthly notions to a luminous station that is a divine station. At this station, man's relationship became one with God. Thus man, instead of considering himself a humble creature of the earth, became an exalted creature.

﴿And teaches them the Book and wisdom﴾ (62:2). This Messenger teaches them the Book, by which these unlettered people also became People of the Book. He teaches them wisdom and makes them aware of the realities of the whole world. Thus they make correct assessments in determining the value of all things, their souls make sound decisions, they adopt right action, and there is no greater wisdom than this.

﴿Although before that they were in clear error﴾ (62:2). Such was the jahiliyyah whose description Ja'far ibn Abi Talib gave to the Negus of Abyssinia. This was when the Quraysh of Makkah sent an embassy to the Negus, consisting of Amr ibn al-As and Abdullah ibn Abi Rabi'ah, in order to paint a horrible picture of the Muslim emigrants before him, to present their position in a distorted light, so that he would expel them from his protection and his land. On that occasion Ja'far said:

"O King! We were an ignorant people. We worshipped idols, ate carrion, committed indecencies, severed ties of kinship, did not care for neighbours, and the strong among us devoured the weak. We were in such circumstances when God sent us a messenger from among us. He called us to call upon the One God and worship Him alone, and to abandon the stones and idols that we and our fathers used to worship. We know his lineage, we know his truthfulness, and we acknowledge his trustworthiness and chastity. He called us to speak the truth, to fulfil trusts, to maintain ties of kinship, to be good to neighbours, and to refrain from unlawful things and bloodshed. He forbade us from every kind of indecency and from falsehood, from consuming the wealth of orphans, and from slandering chaste women. He commanded us to worship God and not associate anything with Him. He enjoined on us prayer, fasting, and zakah."

Despite the fact that they were immersed up to their ears in ignorance and error, God knew well that they were capable of bearing this message. They would be its trustees; their potentials were present within them, and they possessed the capacity required for the new call. Whereas among the Jews, a corruption had arisen in their nature, and the slavery of Egypt had rendered them incapable of reform. A confusion, crookedness, and deviation had come into their psychology. Therefore their reform was no longer possible. They did not become upright in the time of Musa (peace be upon him), nor did they become upright after Musa (peace be upon him), until God decreed curse and wrath upon them, they ceased to be bearers of God's religion in this world, and this honour was taken from them until the Day of Resurrection.

Furthermore, God also knew that in that era the Arabian Peninsula alone could serve as the best center for the Islamic call, and could deliver all humanity from the error of jahiliyyah, because both great empires had corrupted civilization. Their government had been eaten away by decay, and they had been hollowed out from within. The condition was such as Dietz comments upon:

"In the fifth and sixth centuries, the religious world had come close to destruction and ruin, because the beliefs and ideologies that give birth to a civilization had collapsed, and there was no religious ideology present to take the place of the fallen ideologies. It appeared that the civilization and culture whose construction had required mankind four thousand years of labour was about to shatter and disintegrate. Mankind was about to return once again to an age of ignorance, for throughout the world tribes were seen fighting one another. There was no law and no system anywhere in the world. Human civilization was like a vast tree whose broad branches cast their shade over the whole world, but this tree had bent and worms had hollowed it out. In the midst of such all-encompassing corruption, a man appeared who once again gathered all of humanity together."

This man was Prophet Muhammad (ﷺ). This was the condition of humanity from the viewpoint of a European author, but from the Islamic perspective the situation was even darker.

God indeed raised from the Arabian Peninsula this Bedouin nation. It rose bearing the Qur'an and Sunnah, and it possessed the capacity within it. First it reformed itself, and then it changed the destiny of the whole world. God gave this Bedouin people a Messenger and a Book. The Messenger and the Book purified them and gave them wisdom and understanding, although previously they had been in error.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 62, verse 3:

﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them; and He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.﴾ (62:3) Who these "others" are, several narrations have been reported.

Imam al-Bukhari reported from Abdul Aziz ibn Abdullah, who reported from Sulayman ibn Bilal, who reported from Thawr, who reported from Abu al-Ghayth, who reported from Hadrat Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: "We were sitting with the Prophet (ﷺ) when Surah al-Jumu'ah was revealed to him.

﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ (62:3). The Companions (may Allah be pleased with them) asked, 'O Messenger of Allah, who are they?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not answer them, until he was asked three times. Salman al-Farsi was among us. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) placed his blessed hand upon Salman al-Farsi and then said: 'If faith were in the Pleiades, a man or some men from these would attain it.'"

This shows that the people of Persia are included in this verse. Therefore Mujahid says that by it are meant all the non-Arabs who affirmed the Prophet (ﷺ).

Ibn Abi Hatim reported from his father, who reported from Ibrahim ibn al-Ala al-Zubairi, who reported from Walid ibn Muslim, who reported from Abu Muhammad Isa ibn Musa, who reported from Abu Hazim, who reported from Sahl ibn Sa'd al-Sa'idi, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Among some people of my Ummah, from generation to generation, there will be men and women who will enter Paradise without reckoning." Then he recited:

﴿And others among them who have not yet joined them﴾ (62:3), meaning: the people who will come after Muhammad (ﷺ).

Both views have room: the people who are non-Arabs, and those who embraced Islam during the time of the Prophet (ﷺ), as well as their descendants who would be born later. These verses and narrations indicate that this Ummah is one that will endure through successive ages and across all parts of the earth, and it will fulfil this responsibility until the Day of Resurrection. The bearers of this final religion will remain until the end of time.

﴿And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise﴾ (62:3). He is powerful, and has the ability to choose any Ummah for a station; and He is Wise, and knows well for which office they were chosen. And granting ranks to people among the earlier and later generations is also part of His grace and bounty.

This is Allah's bounty; He gives it to whomever He wills, and Allah is the Owner of great bounty. (26:4)

The choosing by Allah of a nation, a community, or an individual for this task, that they should bear this great trust and be a source of Allah's light and grace, and a center where earth and heaven meet, is a very great bounty and favour of Allah. A greater bounty than this is that even if the believer gives his life, his wealth, and everything of this world, it is still more precious than that. The struggle on this path, its hardships, and jihad, in short, all its hardships are more precious and important than anything else.

Allah reminds the Islamic community of Madinah, and those who came after them, and those who walk on the same path, that this is a great bounty and favour upon you, that He has chosen you for this great purpose. He has sent among you a Messenger who purifies you, teaches you the Book and wisdom, and gathers this treasure of knowledge and wisdom for coming generations, and establishes the outstanding deeds of the first Islamic community as a model and example. Allah reminds Muslims that this is the great bounty of God, in comparison with which all worldly and otherworldly rewards are insignificant, while all the material and physical sacrifices made in fulfilling its obligations are also insignificant in comparison with this honour and great bounty.

After this, Allah assures them that the era of the Jews on this earth has ended. They are no longer the bearers of the Divine trust. Neither is this in their hearts, nor is it in their conduct, because the hearts that bear this trust are discerning, understanding, sincere, and practising hearts.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 62, verse 5:**

﴿Those who were charged with the Torah but then failed to bear it are like a donkey carrying books. How evil is the example of the people who deny the signs of Allah. Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (26:5)

The Children of Israel were given the Torah, and they became the bearers of the trust of belief and the Shariah. But they did not

﴿lam yahmilūhā﴾ (26:5), "did not bear it." This trust can only be carried with comprehension (*tafaqquh*), understanding, insight, and wisdom. They abandoned accepting this responsibility, both in the realm of conscience and in the realm of action. The way the Qur'an presents the conduct of the Children of Israel shows that they held this trust in no regard. They were merely carrying a burden. They were not fulfilling the trust and the purposes of the religion.

This is a most contemptible picture that the Holy Qur'an draws of them, yet it expresses their reality in an extremely apt manner.

﴿How evil is the example of the people who denied the signs of Allah. Allah does not guide the wrongdoing people.﴾ (26:5)

Those to whom this final trust has been given, if they adopt the same attitude, then their example is also like this. All those people who were given the religious trust and do not discharge its due, the same ruling applies to them. This includes those Muslims over whom centuries have passed, who merely carry the name of Muslims while lacking the deeds of Muslims. It especially includes those who read the Qur'an and Islamic books but do not perform the obligations contained in them. All these people are like a donkey on which books are loaded. Such people are numerous in our age. The problem is not one of books, study, or teaching, but of action and of taking up responsibilities.

The Jews held, and still hold, the conceit that they are a chosen and preferred nation, the beloved of Allah in preference to all other nations. Other nations, they claimed, are *goyim* (gentiles) or *ummiyyin* (unlettered). Therefore, they are not obliged to act upon the commandments of their religion, which are meant only for the *goyim*.

﴿They say: there is no blame upon us regarding the unlettered.﴾ (3:75) If we commit any injustice against the people of other nations, there is no need for us to be held accountable. This and other similar claims were made by them, and they had no proof for them. Here Allah offers them the challenge of *mubahalah* (mutual invocation of divine curse). This challenge was given to them and also to the Christians.

Say: "O you who have become Jews, if you claim that to the exclusion of all other people you alone are the beloved of Allah, then wish for death, if you are truthful in your claim." But they will never wish for it, because of what their hands have sent ahead, and Allah knows the wrongdoers well. Say: "The death from which you flee will certainly meet you. Then you will be returned to the One who knows the unseen and the manifest, and He will inform you of what you used to do."

Mubahala (the mutual invocation, in which the two parties stand face to face and together pray that Allah destroy whichever of them is upon falsehood) was offered by the Prophet ﷺ to several groups, but none of them came forward out of fear. No one accepted the Prophet's ﷺ challenge to mubahala. This shows that these people were inwardly convinced of the truth of Islam. They knew that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was truthful and that this religion is the true religion.

Imam Ahmad narrated from Isma'il ibn Yazid al-Zarqi, from Abu Yazid, from Furat, from Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas ؓ that Abu Jahl the accursed said: "If I see Muhammad in the Ka'bah, I will attack him until I press his neck down." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Had he done so, the angels would have seized him openly. And if the Jews had wished for death, they would have died, and they would have seen with their own eyes their places in Hell. And if those who were invited by the Messenger of Allah ﷺ to mubahala had come out, then upon returning they would have found neither their wealth nor their families present." (Bukhari, Tirmidhi)

It is also possible that this verse was not a challenge to mubahala for them, but merely a challenge. Since they claimed that they were the beloved and friends of Allah in comparison to other people, why do they not hasten to obtain the blessings with Allah? A friend is eager to meet his friend.

After this, a comment was made on their claim, that they are liars and are not truthful in what they assert. They are not certain that they have done any good deed in the world for the Hereafter, for which they would receive reward. Rather, they have sent forward only evil deeds, because of which they fear death greatly. And one who does not have provisions for the journey does not set out on a journey.

**Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 62, verse 7:**

﴿Wa la yatamannawnahu ................ bil-zalimin﴾ (26:7) "But they will never wish for it, because of the deeds they have already sent ahead, and Allah knows well the wrongdoers."

Now, in the final age, the reality of death is made known to them. Their fear of death is of no benefit. Death is a certain matter, and there is nothing to fear from it. It does no harm. After death, one must return to Allah, and then there is an account and reckoning before Allah, about which there is no doubt.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 62, verse 8:

﴿Say, "Indeed, the death from which you flee will surely meet you. Then you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do."﴾ (26:8)

This is a notice of attention, addressed to the Muslims and to non-Muslims alike, to refresh this reality in their hearts and minds. People forget this inescapable truth, or try to make themselves forget it: death is coming. This life is going to end. However much you flee from it in this world, you will end up in the jaws of death. Therefore there is no place of refuge other than Allah; there is no place to escape from giving account before Him. So there is no benefit in fleeing from it.

Tabarani, in his Mu'jam, narrates the hadith of Mu'adh ibn Muhammad al-Hudhali, from Yunus, from al-Hasan, from Hadrat Samurah (may Allah be pleased with him), in its marfu' form, that: "The one who flees from death is like a fox from which the earth was demanding its debt. It began to run, until, exhausted from running and unable to continue, it entered its burrow. There the earth said to it: 'O fox, my debt?'"

Now comes the final closing portion of this surah, which concerns the Friday prayer. This is in relation to an occurrence that took place; such an event may have happened more than once, since the wording indicates that it used to happen repeatedly.

The Friday prayer cannot be offered without congregation. It is necessary that Muslims gather for it, listen to the Friday sermon (khutbah), and that the sermon impart religious instruction to the Muslims. It is a religious and organizational gathering of Muslims, in which religion, worldly life and the Hereafter are all brought together in one sequence of assembly, and all these matters are part of worship. Through the Friday prayer, the collective outlook and system of Islam become clearly evident. Countless ahadith have been transmitted concerning it, in which the virtue of Friday, its preparation, bathing (ghusl), cleanliness of clothing and the application of perfume have been enjoined.

In the Sahihayn, it is related from Hadrat Ibn Umar (رضي الله عنه) that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said:

Idha ja'a ahadukum al-jumu'ah falyaghtasil (إذا جاء أحدكم الجمعة فليغتسل) "When any of you comes to Friday prayer, he should perform ghusl."

The compilers of the four Sunan have narrated the hadith of Aws ibn Aws al-Thaqafi. He says: I heard from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that whoever bathes on the day of Friday and applies perfume, if it is available to him, and wears good clothes, then goes out toward the mosque, and if he wishes to offer voluntary prayer, he offers it, and does not cause harm to anyone in the mosque; then he sits down in the mosque until the imam emerges and he leads the prayer, that Friday will be expiation for the sins between it and the next Friday."

﴿O you who believe! When the call is proclaimed for prayer on the day of Friday, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade.﴾ That is, cease all worldly activities and occupy yourselves with the remembrance of Allah.

﴿That is better for you, if you only knew.﴾

This indicates that, abandoning all the interests of life, spend a little time in the remembrance of Allah, abandoning economic activities here.

The phrase ﴿hasten to the remembrance of Allah﴾ means that before the Friday prayer you should be occupied with remembrance and reflection, pure remembrance of Allah, and connect your relationship at that time with the higher world. In this way you will attain purification of the heart, and as a result of this remembrance, the fragrant perfume of the higher world and the gentle breezes of the fragrant wind will leave their impression upon the heart. And then, in the pursuit of livelihood too, the remembrance of Allah and the bounty of Allah...

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 62, verse 10:

﴿Then when the prayer is concluded, disperse in the land and seek the bounty of Allah, and remember Allah often, that you may be successful.﴾ (62:10)

This is the balance of the Islamic system: a balance between the necessities of worldly life, such as work and the pursuit of livelihood, and the occupation of the soul with the remembrance of Allah. For a time, one should step away from the activities of seeking a livelihood, sit in seclusion, and engage in remembrance (dhikr) and reflection (fikr). This is essential for the life of the heart, and without this spiritual and inner growth, no person can fulfil the great trust (amanah) that is the responsibility of a Muslim. The remembrance of Allah is also necessary during the pursuit of livelihood. Indeed, if remembrance and reflection accompany the pursuit of livelihood, that pursuit itself becomes worship ('ibadah). Yet, apart from remembrance and reflection during one's livelihood, it is also necessary to set aside a time purely for remembrance and reflection, in which there is no other occupation, as these two verses indicate.

When Hadrat 'Urak ibn Malik (may Allah be pleased with him) would finish the Friday prayer, he would stand at the door of the mosque and say: "O Allah, I have responded to Your call, I have performed the obligatory prayer, and now I am leaving the mosque as You have commanded. O Allah, grant me Your bounty. You are the best of those who provide sustenance." (Ibn Abi Hatim). This shows how seriously those people took the command of Allah, and with what simplicity, because they had a consciousness in their hearts that the Qur'an contains the commands of Allah and that Muslims must carry them out.

This simple understanding of the Companions, their serious conduct, and their conversing with their Lord with great simplicity were the factors that enabled them to rise to such a lofty station, even though they had come out of jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance), and the habits and inclinations of jahiliyyah constantly pulled them towards themselves. An example of one habit of jahiliyyah is presented in the final verses of this surah.

﴿When they saw a trade or a diversion, they rushed towards it and left you standing. Say: What is with Allah is better than diversion and trade, and Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (26 : 11)

It is narrated from Jabir that once, while we were praying behind the Prophet (ﷺ), a caravan arrived carrying food. The people rushed towards the caravan, and only two men remained with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). They were Abu Bakr and Umar (رضي الله عنهما). At that time this verse was revealed:

﴿When they saw a trade or a diversion, they rushed towards it and left you standing.﴾

The verse indicates that what is with Allah is better than that frivolity and trade, and it also states explicitly that Allah is among the best of providers.

﴿And Allah is the best of providers.﴾ (26 : 11)

This verse shows how much effort Islam put into the training and education of the Bedouin Arab society, and how it prepared from those people the community of Companions (Sahabah) who created a record in human history, one for which there is no parallel in all of human history. Their lives are an example for those who carry out the work of the Islamic call (da'wah) in later times, showing with what patience and perseverance these people acted, and how they endured and overcame the weaknesses, defects, shortcomings and lapses that arose on the path of the Islamic revolution. Today we too can reform ourselves in the same way. The human soul has the capacity for good as well as for evil. It has the potential to reach the highest levels of spiritual strength and spiritual and inner purity, which have no limit. But for this, patience and steadfastness, understanding and insight, firmness and perseverance, and continuous struggle are needed. A person should not become disheartened and turn back halfway. And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe.
